newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares close higher after early rally.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares close higher after early rally.

text.p: The Cairo bourse regained its footing on Thursday when shares rallied, lifting the index to its highest level in a week marked mostly by slipping prices.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose three percent or 10.73 points to 381.42 points. Turnover was 65.29 million ($19.23 million).
Signs of a recovery first appeared on Wednesday, when shares rebounded on buying initiated by a handful of investors.

International securities house INGBarings said: "The rise...was in a way an over-reaction, although it may provide an indication of future movements in the index. The stock market may yet prove to be relatively volatile on the movement of relatively small flows of capital."
Out of the 86 shares traded on Thursday, 57 gained while just eight lost. Twenty-one ended unchanged.
The top five shares in turnover value terms closed higher.

"It is interesting to note that so many stocks in the top 40 by market capitalisation rose by over four percent (on Wednesday)," ING Barings said. "It is clear that there will continue to be problems in the market due to liquidity constraints, which, when there is demand, will lead to larger share prices rises than are warranted fundamentally."
The cement sector siphoned up much of the turnover, with Suez Cement closing 3.44 pounds up at 72.42 in turnover worth 7.6 million pounds.
Helwan Portland Cement was busy again in 5.4 million pounds of turnover. Its share closed higher by 1.25 pounds at 78.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development jumped 18.5 pounds to a 488.5 close in 5 million trade.
Commercial International Bank closed higher four pounds at 84.06 in 4.5 million pounds of trade.
Brokers have said a "buy" recommendation for the bank's global depositary receipt offering from Barings was behind the increased activity.
The index for openly traded firms perked up on Thursday and ended at 600.88 from 575.37 points the previous day. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 260.88 from 255.88.
